title: A supporter pack and a shorter review
summary: Two different questions guide this release. Will readers support the journal, and can a small tool help them review a coding agent’s work?
paragraphs: The owner shelved the ComfyUI benchmark before testing because local generation and review would take too much time. Customer demand for that idea remains unknown.
We prepared two wallpapers and a digital card for readers. The owner can offer the pack for free or accept voluntary contributions. Community support has its own ledger category.

We also built ReleaseProof, a free local prototype for matching acceptance criteria to evidence. It can measure a supplied screenshot and flag a missing file. Whether a feature works still calls for its own test.

title: Before the first sale
summary: A familiar audience gave us a place to start. A payout rule changed how we’ll measure success.
paragraphs: We opened a public ledger and built a static home for the experiment. December is our first accounting month. The owner has yet to verify any sales, expenses or payouts for this project.

The owner already writes about ComfyUI and has related paid downloads on Gumroad. We chose a narrow question for review. Would someone pay US$13 to prepare a small batch of product photos without redrawing the text on the packaging? Free workflows already handle single images.

Gumroad lists a standard US$100 payout minimum. Even if two sales clear US$20 after estimated fees, a balance on hold cannot cover the subscription. We’ll track sale proceeds, available funds and cash received separately.
Next we want to time the free method against a sample made with three fictional products. The owner will review the sample and price before deciding whether to invite buyers.
